title: Necessity 1: Мне надо (the dative subject)
description: To say 'I have to' in Russian, the person goes into the DATIVE: Мне надо... / Мне нужно..., not 'я надо.' Надо and нужно are impersonal and never agree with anyone.
descriptionRussian: Чтобы сказать «мне нужно что-то сделать», человек ставится в ДАТЕЛЬНЫЙ падеж: Мне надо... / Мне нужно..., а не «я надо». Надо и нужно безличны и ни с кем не согласуются.
intro: Saying you need something in Russian starts by removing yourself from the subject slot. There is no subject at all in these sentences: the structure is impersonal, and you appear in the dative as the person the need belongs to. If you did the dative book this is a familiar move. If not, it is the error worth killing first.
rules: Надо and нужно are impersonal ('it is necessary'). They have NO subject and never change form for gender or number.
The person who feels the need goes into the DATIVE case: Мне надо работать, NOT «я надо работать». This is the error to kill first.
Dative pronouns to memorize: я → мне, ты → тебе, он → ему, она → ей, мы → нам, вы → вам, они → им.
The pattern is three slots: dative person + надо/нужно + infinitive. Мне надо отдохнуть. Нам нужно купить хлеб.
Надо and нужно are near-synonyms. Надо is a bit more colloquial, нужно a bit more neutral; both express plain necessity and are usually interchangeable.
examples: Мне надо работать. (I have to work.) Person 'я' → dative мне, NOT 'я надо'.
Тебе нужно отдохнуть. (You need to rest.) ты → тебе.
Ей надо позвонить маме. (She has to call mom.) она → ей.
Нам нужно купить хлеб. (We need to buy bread.) мы → нам.
Лене надо встать рано. (Lena needs to get up early.) Лена → Лене, the noun goes dative too.
Антону нужно отдохнуть. (Anton needs to rest.) Антон → Антону.

tables.title: Dative of the person + надо/нужно + infinitive

items.hint: Надо has no subject. The person who must do something goes into the dative.
items.explanation: This is the core rule. Надо is impersonal, so 'I' is not the subject. The person goes into the dative: я → мне. «Я надо работать» is the classic mistake; the correct form is Мне надо работать.
Нужно works exactly like надо: impersonal, person in the dative. Ты → тебе. Тебе нужно отдохнуть, never «ты нужно».

items.hint: Dative of 'она' is one short word.
items.explanation: она → ей in the dative. Ей надо позвонить маме.
мы → нам in the dative. Нам нужно купить хлеб. The infinitive купить (perfective) marks a single completed errand.

items.promptEnglish: Lena needs to get up early.
items.hint: Nouns follow the same rule: the person goes dative. Лена is feminine -а.
items.explanation: Nouns behave like pronouns here. Лена is feminine ending in -а, so the dative is Лене (-а → -е). Лене надо встать рано. Not «Лена надо».
они → им in the dative. Им нужно подождать.

blanks: _____ надо позвонить врачу. (Anton has to call the doctor.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The person who must do something goes into the dative, even when it is a name. Антон is masculine consonant: dative + -у → Антону. Антону надо позвонить, not «Антон надо».

errorCorrection.explanation: Надо is impersonal and has no subject, so 'he' cannot stand in the nominative. The person who must act goes into the dative: он becomes ему.
Нужно is impersonal, so the person who needs to rest takes the dative: вы becomes вам. Вы is the nominative, a form the impersonal нужно never allows.
Надо takes the dative person, not the nominative: Антон becomes Антону. Антон is the nominative subject form that the impersonal надо has no room for.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton needs to rest after work.
errorCorrection.explanation: A noun naming the necessity-feeler goes into the dative just like a pronoun. Нужно is impersonal, so Антон cannot stay nominative: a masculine consonant noun adds -у, giving Антону. Correct: Антону нужно отдохнуть после работы.

The necessity-feeler takes the DATIVE, not the accusative. Машу is the accusative ('он видит Машу'), but with нужно the person is not an object: they are the one for whom the action is necessary, so the dative Маше is required.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: He has to get up early.
errorCorrection.explanation: Надо is impersonal, so 'he' takes the dative: он becomes ему. Он is the nominative, the classic «он надо» mistake. Correct: Ему надо рано вставать.

minimalPairs.explanation: Надо is impersonal: the person goes into the dative, never the nominative. Я → мне. «Я надо» is wrong; Мне надо работать is correct. This is THE error to eliminate.
Нужно behaves like надо. Он → ему in the dative. Ему нужно поесть. The nominative «он нужно» does not work, because нужно has no subject to agree with.

reviewVocab.definition: it is necessary / one has to (impersonal predicatives). The person who must act goes into the dative; надо and нужно never change form.
reviewVocab.example: Мне надо работать. Нам нужно купить хлеб.

reviewVocab.term: мне, тебе, ему, ей, нам, вам, им
reviewVocab.definition: dative forms of the personal pronouns. With надо/нужно, the necessity-feeler takes one of these, not the nominative (я, ты, он...).
reviewVocab.example: Ей надо отдохнуть. Им нужно подождать.

reviewVocab.definition: the correct frame for 'I have to': dative person + надо + infinitive. «Я надо» is the most common beginner mistake.
